content: Agent Zero's MCP server initialization was fire-and-forget — initialize_mcp() returned a DeferredTask but never called result_sync(), causing "Tool carabiner_db not found" when agents interacted before the subprocess finished registering tools. Fixed by awaiting init like initialize_chats() already does. Root cause pattern: async init without await at startup.

Menu API returned empty array despite 4 rows in workspace_menu because Pydantic MenuOut schema typed `recipe` as Optional[Dict] but one record had a plain JSON string in the JSONB column. Pydantic rejected it, the try/except in the Flask blueprint silently swallowed the error and returned []. Fix: widen type to Optional[Dict | str]. Lesson: JSONB columns can store any valid JSON — strings, arrays, objects — so Pydantic schemas must match the actual data variance, not just the intended type.

CarabinerOS Flask blueprint catches all exceptions in API handlers and returns _empty_response() (empty JSON array []), hiding real errors behind "no data" UI states. This made the menu Pydantic validation bug invisible — the page showed "No menu items yet" instead of an error. Debug required checking Docker logs for the actual traceback. Pattern to watch: bare except returning success-shaped responses masks bugs as missing data.

CarabinerOS has two parallel table systems: operational tables (models.py: menu_items, items, etc.) and workspace tables (workspace_models.py: workspace_menu, workspace_inventory, etc.). The frontend API reads from workspace_* tables. The MCP tools also read from workspace_* tables via repositories.py. Seed data lives in Alembic migration 002. When debugging "no data" issues, always check WHICH table system the endpoint queries — data in one doesn't imply data in the other.

CarabinerOS action cards redesigned from flat Sheet list to kitchen-ticket solitaire grid (2-col) because user feedback said it looked like "another Claude website." Chose Kitchen Display System aesthetic — left-border station colors, monospace labels, "Tickets/FIRE/Cleared" vocabulary — over generic dashboard cards because restaurant operators recognize KDS patterns instinctively.

Chose inline card expansion with Framer Motion layoutId over AnimatePresence view-swap because user wanted "pick card from table, flip it, bring close to face" — not a separate page slide. layoutId enables shared-layout animation between collapsed and expanded states within the same ScrollArea.

When running parallel agents where Agent B does a full rewrite of files Agent A also patches, resolve merge conflicts by taking Agent B's version — the rewrite subsumes the patches. Confirmed this pattern when Agent A fixed CSS on action-card-expanded.tsx and Agent B rewrote it entirely. Agent B's version already incorporated the same fixes organically.

Action card chat pre-fill uses a type+module lookup map (e.g., "urgent+inventory" → "Want me to place an emergency order?") with quick-action chips above the input. Chips auto-send on click. This pattern — contextual suggestions based on card metadata — was validated by the user as "goated" because it reduces friction from free-text to one-tap action.

rune:team orchestrator failed with "unknown option '-m'" when spawning sub-agents via CLI. Workaround: dispatch agents directly using the Agent tool with isolation:"worktree" and run_in_background:true instead of going through rune:team's CLI-based dispatch.
